title: Circadian PERIOD proteins regulate TC-DSB repair through anchoring to the nuclear envelope.
authors: Le Bozec, Benjamin; Guitton-Sert, Laure; Collins, Sarah; Finoux, Anne-Laure; Payrault, Charlotte; Guillou, Emmanuelle; Aguirrebengoa, Marion; Dougados, Vanessa; Jouffret, Virginie; Frison, Jessica; Carette, Romane; Rocher, Vincent; Arnould, Coline; Guenole, Aude; Lazar, Ikrame; Marnef, Aline; Frit, Philippe; Calsou, Patrick; Mangeat, Thomas; Puget, Nadine; Legube, Gaelle
one_liner_zh: 该文研究昼夜节律PERIOD蛋白在转录偶联DSB修复中锚定核膜的作用，属DNA修复生物学，未涉及蛋白质-DNA结合建模、AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Repair of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) produced in transcriptionally active chromatin occurs through a poorly characterized pathway called transcription-coupled DSB repair (TC-DSBR). Here, using a screening approach scoring multiple outputs in human cells, we identified proteins from the PERIOD complex, ensuring circadian oscillations, as previously unknown TC-DSBR players. We show that PER2 is recruited at TC-DSBs and contributes to their targeting to the nuclear envelope (NE), where SUN1 and the nuclear pore complex (NPC) act as docking sites. TC-DSB anchoring at the NE fosters RAD51 assembly and prevents DSB clustering and translocations. In agreement, the circadian clock regulates TC-DSB targeting to the NE, RAD51 assembly, and DSB clustering. Our study shows a direct link between the circadian rhythm and the response to DSBs in transcribed genes, opening strategies for chrono-chemotherapies based on topoisomerase poisons that induce DSBs in active loci.
abstract_zh: 转录活跃染色质中产生的DNA双链断裂（DSBs）的修复通过一种称为转录偶联DSB修复（TC-DSBR）的、特征尚不明确的途径进行。在此，我们利用一种在人类细胞中评分多种输出的筛选方法，鉴定出PERIOD复合体中的蛋白质（确保昼夜节律振荡）为先前未知的TC-DSBR参与者。我们显示PER2被招募至TC-DSBs，并促进其靶向核膜（NE），其中SUN1和核孔复合体（NPC）作为对接位点。TC-DSB在核膜上的锚定促进RAD51组装，并防止DSB聚集和易位。与此一致，昼夜节律调节TC-DSB向核膜的靶向、RAD51组装及DSB聚集。我们的研究揭示了昼夜节律与转录基因中DSB反应之间的直接联系，为基于拓扑异构酶毒物（在活跃位点诱导DSB）的时辰化疗策略开辟了途径。
